newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait minister confident ahead of MPs' questions.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait minister confident ahead of MPs' questions.

text.p: Kuwait's Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan said on Wednesday he would stick to the truth if he were challenged in parliament over his supervision of key economic bodies.

"Through truth and honesty, I will be able to answer all that would come in this interpellation," Nasser al-Rodhan told reporters at parliament after a meeting with the house's financial affairs committee.
Rodhan chairs the Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA), which manages the state's foreign investments of about $40 billion, the Central Bank and Kuwait Airways.
Three opposition MPs are planning to submit a request to question Rodhan over alleged violations by institutions that fall under his jurisdiction, MPs say.
The measure would be the first if its kind since the election of the current house in October 1996.

A parliamentary source said Rodhan would be asked about suspected lack of action on alleged violations by some of the institutions he oversees, noting that Rodhan was not suspected of involvement "wrongdoings of criminal nature."

Al-Talea weekly newspaper quoted Parliamentarian Sami al-Munayes, a member of the Kuwait Democratic Forum (KDF) opposition grouping and one of the MPs who signed the request, as saying the aim was to determine Rodhan's resposibility for not implementing some laws.
Talea, the KDF mouthpiece, said on Wednesday the interpellation would "reveal through documents the shortcomings in Nasser al-Rodhan's performance."
